title: Open GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code
summary: GitHub Copilot is the coding assistant inside the editor. This exercise connects the desktop editor to your GitHub account and explains a tiny practice file.
where: On Mac or Windows obtain Visual Studio Code at code.visualstudio.com and sign in with the GitHub account authorized for Copilot.
These exact status-bar and folder-picker steps use desktop VS Code. An iPad browser does not supply the same local desktop editor.

actions.title: Open a practice folder
actions.do: Create AI-Editor-Practice in Documents using Finder or File Explorer. In VS Code choose File → Open Folder and select that folder.
actions.see: Explorer in the left sidebar shows AI-Editor-Practice.
actions.stuck: If you opened an individual file, repeat Open Folder so the editor knows the project boundary.

actions.title: Sign in to Copilot
actions.do: Hover over the Copilot status icon and select Use AI Features or Sign in to use Copilot. Follow the browser sign-in and return to VS Code.
actions.see: The editor shows an active Copilot account or offers an eligible plan.
actions.stuck: For a managed subscription, confirm which GitHub account holds the seat. A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is a different product.

actions.title: Make a sample
actions.do: Choose File → New Text File. Type “Queue target: 15 minutes.” Save it inside the folder as service.txt.
actions.see: service.txt appears in Explorer and the sentence is visible in the editor.
actions.stuck: If the file opens as Untitled, use Save As and select the practice folder explicitly.

actions.title: Ask about the active file
actions.do: Open the Chat view and ask “Read service.txt. What is the target and unit? Please leave the file unchanged.” Add the file as context if prompted.
actions.see: The answer gives 15 minutes.
actions.stuck: If it cannot see service.txt, open it or attach it through the chat’s context picker and ask again.

roles: Read a small mail-operations script or note.
Explain an inventory helper from the editor.
Learn what code in an app does.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Try one inline suggestion in VS Code
summary: Inline suggestions appear as dim text while you type. You control what becomes part of the file.
where: Open desktop VS Code on Mac or Windows with GitHub Copilot enabled. A text file saved with a .js extension is enough for this exercise.

actions.title: Start a JavaScript file
actions.do: In a practice folder create double.js. Type the comment “// Return twice a numeric value” and press Enter.
actions.see: The file tab ends in .js and the comment is visible.
actions.stuck: If the tab says Plain Text at the bottom, save with the .js extension or set the language to JavaScript.

actions.title: Trigger a suggestion
actions.do: Type “function doubleValue(n) {” and press Enter. Pause briefly and look for dim suggested code.
actions.see: A completion may propose a return statement. Its exact spelling can vary.
actions.stuck: If nothing appears, check the Copilot status menu and use the editor’s trigger-inline-suggestion command.

actions.title: Decide what to insert
actions.do: If the suggestion computes twice n, press Tab to accept it. Use Escape to dismiss an unsuitable suggestion, then type return n * 2; yourself. Add the closing brace if needed.
actions.see: Accepted text becomes regular editor text.
actions.stuck: If Tab merely indents, there was no active completion. Trigger another suggestion or finish typing the line.

actions.title: Check the logic
actions.do: Open Chat and ask “Read double.js and explain the results for 3, 0 and -2.” Compare each prediction to the expression in the file.
actions.see: The expected values are 6, 0 and -4.
actions.stuck: If the values differ, inspect what was actually inserted. Highlighted or dim text may still be a suggestion.

roles: Complete small reporting helpers.
Complete transformations in a local sample script.
Try a single function without turning a whole task over to an agent.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Use Copilot Chat to explain a boundary
summary: Ask a question with an answer you can verify, then change one character and see whether the explanation follows the code.
where: Use the desktop VS Code Chat view while signed into GitHub Copilot. Open a practice folder with permission to create files.

actions.title: Create a rule
actions.do: Save a new file named rule.js in your folder with the single line “const isReady = count => count >= 3;”. Type the line without quotation marks.
actions.see: You can see the greater-than-or-equal sign and the number 3.
actions.stuck: If the file shows special quotation marks, remove them. They are not part of this sample.

actions.title: Supply the source
actions.do: Open Chat. Attach rule.js with the context control or use the open file as context. Type “Read rule.js and explain the threshold. Give results for 2, 3 and 4. Make no edits.”
actions.see: The answer gives false, true and true.
actions.stuck: If the answer says “more than 3,” ask which operator appears in the actual file.

actions.title: Make one edit yourself
actions.do: Change >= to >, save the file and leave it open. Ask for the same three results from the saved revision.
actions.see: Only the middle result changes, to false.
actions.stuck: If all three are identical to the earlier answer, reattach the saved file or start a fresh chat with it.

actions.title: Explain the difference
actions.do: Ask which single input distinguishes the two rules and why. Compare the response with both versions you typed.
actions.see: A count of exactly 3 separates the rules.
actions.stuck: If the response introduces a real workplace policy, remind it that the entire rule is the one-line exercise.

roles: Review a quota threshold in an Exchange script.
Understand a group-size filter.
Check an app’s boundary rule.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Open the work version of Copilot
summary: Use your work account to turn a short sample notice into a question and answer.
where: On Mac, PC or iPad, open m365.cloud.microsoft/chat in a browser. Choose your work or school account. The Microsoft 365 Copilot mobile app also offers work chat when available.

actions.title: Choose your account
actions.do: Open the site and select Sign in if asked. Choose the account your organization gave you.
actions.see: A work Copilot home or Chat opens. Some accounts have a newer Home layout.
actions.stuck: Check the account picture. If it shows your personal account, switch accounts or use a separate browser profile.

actions.title: Find the writing box
actions.do: Choose Chat or New if needed. Click the box where you can type a message.
actions.see: A text cursor appears.
actions.stuck: If sign-in succeeds but chat is unavailable, check your work license or ask the account administrator.

actions.title: Send a first question
actions.do: Enter “Sample notice: shared mailbox search resumes at 14:00 UTC. Delivery continues. Which feature is affected?”
actions.see: The answer identifies search. The notice says delivery continues.
actions.stuck: If it starts searching the web, ask it to use only the sample notice.

actions.title: Check a missing fact
actions.do: Ask “What is the name of the person handling the change?”
actions.see: The source gives no name.
actions.stuck: Ask it to quote the source for any name. Work grounding and account permissions determine which outside evidence a real work chat can use.

roles: Read a supplied mail notice.
Check a rollout message for missing facts.
Turn a feature description into test questions.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Find a summary in Outlook
summary: Copilot can summarize an email conversation and point you back to the contributing messages.
where: Open Outlook on your Mac, PC or mobile device and choose a work mailbox with Copilot access. For an all-fictional exercise, open work Copilot Chat instead and paste the sample thread below.

actions.title: Locate the summary button
actions.do: Open an existing non-sensitive conversation you can read. Look above the messages for Summary by Copilot or Summarize.
actions.see: The control appears on supported Outlook versions and accounts.
actions.stuck: If it is missing, use Copilot Chat for the sample task. That practices the reading skill without demonstrating the Outlook button.

actions.title: Inspect one source
actions.do: For the Outlook route select the summary. Follow one numbered reference if the summary includes any.
actions.see: The reference points to an underlying email.
actions.stuck: If there are no references, expand the original messages and check the latest substantive reply manually.

actions.title: Try a sample in chat
actions.do: Paste “M1 Kim: Tuesday confirmed. M2 Sam: Could we use Wednesday? M3 Kim: I will check. State the confirmed and requested days.”
actions.see: Tuesday is confirmed. Wednesday is requested.
actions.stuck: If it says Wednesday is booked, ask for the exact words that accept it.

actions.title: Draft one line
actions.do: Ask “Write a reply asking for the decision. Show only the draft.”
actions.see: A suitable draft asks whether Wednesday is confirmed.
actions.stuck: Read the draft as if you were the recipient. A new assertion of approval would undo the original check.

roles: Follow a maintenance approval back to its email.
Resolve the status of a rollout request.
Separate a user suggestion from an accepted change.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Read a meeting recap in Teams
summary: A recap brings together available meeting evidence. Learn where to check whether a decision appears in the record.
where: In Teams, open a past meeting you already have permission to view. To practice without a real meeting, use m365.cloud.microsoft/chat and the two sample lines below.

actions.title: Find the recap
actions.do: Open the meeting chat and look for Recap. Open it and look for Copilot where your account permits it.
actions.see: A supported meeting may show notes, a transcript and a Copilot panel.
actions.stuck: If that panel is missing, use the sample below. A missing transcript limits later questions about spoken words.

actions.title: Read before trusting
actions.do: If a transcript is available, inspect a sentence with its speaker and time.
actions.see: You can separate text from the meeting chat from words captured during the meeting.
actions.stuck: A transcript started late covers only the captured portion. Treat earlier discussion as unknown unless another source records it.

actions.title: Run a small exercise
actions.do: In Chat paste “10:01 Jo: I propose Friday. 10:05 Pat: Monday approved. List the proposed day and approved day with evidence.”
actions.see: The two days are Friday and Monday.
actions.stuck: If the tool combines the days, ask for one row per sentence.

actions.title: Check the owner
actions.do: Ask “Who agreed to do the work?”
actions.see: The excerpt identifies an approver but names no person who accepted the assignment.
actions.stuck: If it assigns the job to Pat, request the words in which Pat accepted the work.

roles: Check spoken incident handoffs.
Track a rollout decision to its evidence.
Write issues from a design discussion.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Ask Excel to check a small table
summary: Give Copilot numbers that you can add yourself before you try a larger workbook.
where: Open Excel with an eligible account and make a practice workbook. Use the Copilot control if shown. For chat-only access, put the same rows into work Copilot Chat.

actions.title: Enter the data
actions.do: In A1 type Team and in B1 type Count. Add North and 4 in row 2, then South and 7 in row 3.
actions.see: The sheet has one header and two data rows.
actions.stuck: If you are in chat, type “Team, Count / North, 4 / South, 7.”

actions.title: Ask for an explicit formula
actions.do: Select the data, open Copilot and ask “What formula adds these two counts? Which cells does it use?”
actions.see: A suitable answer uses =SUM(B2:B3).
actions.stuck: If the workbook controls are unavailable, type the suggested formula into B4 yourself.

actions.title: Read the cell
actions.do: Check B4 or the answer against 4 + 7.
actions.see: The total is 11.
actions.stuck: If the result is 4 or 7, check whether both numeric cells are in the formula range.

actions.title: Change one row
actions.do: Replace 7 with 9. Recheck the total. For the chat fallback send the revised values again.
actions.see: In a working sheet the calculated total becomes 13.
actions.stuck: A plain chat shows a new answer only after you give it the new data. If the sheet still says 11, inspect the B4 formula.

roles: Check a supplied mailbox count.
Validate a small adoption report.
Test a simple scoreboard calculation.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work
